chapter_theme: Knower, knowing and known (ஞாதுரு, ஞானம், ஞேயம்): for one who stands in Siva as the known, the bonds and the ego lose their hold and the two of 'I' and 'He' become one. Tirumular speaks of Nandi as the guru who reworked his tattvas, broke his ignorance and showed him a state beyond the senses; silence and the mudras complete the knower.
structure_note: Three verses on standing in the known (1605 to 1607), three in the first person on what Nandi did (1608 to 1610, each ending நந்தியே), and three on silence, mudra and the knower (1611 to 1613).

1605.reading: For one who stands in the known, the unfailing bliss of Siva, the bonds that cling do not spread, and even if they spread, once the ego is gone and one holds that state, the unfailing state of nectar is reached.
1605.nuance: ஞேயம், what is to be known, is here Siva himself as the bliss that does not leave. The verse allows that bonds may still arise (படரினும்) and makes the loss of ஆங்காரம், the ego, the condition. அமுத நிலை may be the deathless state or the yogic nectar of earlier chapters; both readings stand.

1606.reading: For those who stand in the known, knowledge and the rest follow; the knower of the known finds release in the known, and those who reach the known of the known know the knowledge that stands in the gathering.
1606.nuance: The verse turns ஞேயம் over five times, and the phrases (ஞேயத்தின் ஞாதுரு, ஞேயத்தின் ஞேயம்) resist a fixed sense. ஆயம் may be the assembly of the tattvas, the soul's faculties, or the company of the knowers; I cannot fix which.

1607.reading: The reality appears as two, 'self' and 'He'; seeing both within oneself and offering the flower called 'self' at His feet, one finds that saying 'I' and 'He' is no longer right.
1607.nuance: The self offered as a flower turns outer worship into an inner act. The last line, நல்லது ஒன்று அன்றே, can be read as 'is no good thing' (duality is wrong) or as the rhetorical 'is it not the one good thing'; the first fits the verse's movement from two to one, but the second is not ruled out.

1608.reading: Nandi changed the thirty-six tattvas set in me and set me anew, laid the Supreme's all-pervading nature over me to be praised, made it sure, made me Siva, and through the known destroyed my fear and took me as his own.
1608.nuance: வாறாறு is read as ஆறாறு, six sixes, the thirty-six tattvas. வியாத்துவம் is vyaptva, pervasion. Nandi is both Tirumular's guru and a name of Siva; the verse lets the two stand together.

1609.reading: Nandi broke through the ignorance in my later knowledge, which was like that of fools who never knew, made me the Supreme so that I might know myself, and stayed, making me know myself in his own Siva-state.
1609.nuance: The first two lines are hard: முன்னை அறிவு and பின்னை அறிவு may be the soul's knowledge before and after the guru's work, or before and after birth. தற்சிவம் is taken as Siva's own state. The third line is misprinted in the source.

1610.reading: Nandi came and showed me, saying 'see': an eye that does not see, a hearing that does not hear, an enjoyment that does not swerve, a union that is no joining, a modesty that feels no shame, and the awareness at nada's end.
1610.nuance: Each phrase pairs a faculty with its negation, so the state shown is one where seeing, hearing, enjoying and joining go on without the senses or a second party. நாதாந்தம், the end of nada, is a technical term for the stage beyond primal sound.

1611.reading: For those to whom silence has come, release comes too, the powers stand before them, all speech ends in a mute word, and the five acts come forward.
1611.nuance: மோனம் கைவந்தோர் is those for whom silence has become natural, not merely those who keep a vow of speech. Line 3 (வந்தூமை யாமொழி) is read as ஊமையாம் மொழி, a speech that is mute; it can also be split to mean they become mute and speech ends. That the five acts, the Lord's work, 'come forward' for them is a strong claim and may mean they share in it.

1612.reading: Those who, through the three mudras, turned back the kala and breath set in the three by a fourfold measure, and cut off their bondage at the bright guru's feet in that bliss, are neither born nor die.
1612.nuance: The three mudras, the three in which they end, and the fourfold measure (நான்மடங்கு) of kala and breath are technical and unnamed. பெத்தம் is baddha, the bound state, which the verse sets against release. Only the conclusion, freedom from birth and death at the guru's feet, is plain.

1613.reading: The supreme knower holds the mudra nurtured by abundant Shakti, the three higher forms; entering the known, the resounding dance, he stands as the root-form, the one called the knower.
1613.nuance: மேலைச் சொரூபங்கள் மூன்று are not named; they may be three forms of Siva or three states beyond the waking ones. ஆலித்த நட்டம் (the roaring or resounding dance) is made the known itself, so the dance is what the knower enters. மூலச் சொரூபன் may be the knower or Siva; the verse ends by naming him ஞாதுரு.

links.note: Both make silence the mark of the finished state: 1611 says silence brings release and powers, 1634 that chant and sound are no longer needed once samadhi is in hand.

source_issues: 1609 line 3 reads தன்aன, a Latin letter for ன; read தன்னை.
1611 line 3 (மோனங்கை வந்தூமை யாமொழி) can be split more than one way.
